items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)

items.author: Claude (BL-744 stage 2 field re-measure)
items.title: A processor never buys inputs worth more than its output - the anchor carried to live prices
items.design:
THE FINDING (BL-744 stage 2, 2026-09-02). With every recipe clearing the margin anchor at base price, the industrial field still collapses by tick 25 of an unwarmed lapse: expenditure runs 1.5-2.5x income from tick 4, corps go into debt, exit twelve quarters later, and the survivors are idled by their own agency. The anchor is evaluated at BASE; the sim runs at the CEILING - processed goods are ceiled in every market (10x base), so a processor pays up to 10x for inputs its recipe values at 2x, loses on every batch, and is idled as 'persistently loss-making'. Idling it removes supply, which keeps the ceiling on, which idles the next one. The ancient band takes the same wave and recovers because its chains are shallow; the industrial mid-chain (silicon, refined_copper, electronics) does not.

THE DESIGN, in the anchor's own terms: a processor's input purchase (pool bid, BL-654; auto-demand) is capped so that Σ inputs at the bid price <= output value at the current price minus the wage per batch - the M1 identity carried from authoring time to the live tick. Above the cap it does not buy and runs at the supply scalar it has (the shortfall rule: scale down, never idle - PRODUCTION.md). This is a per-recipe reservation ceiling in place of the flat reservation_mult (9x base) for processing inputs; the flat one stays for upkeep goods. It must be pure and deterministic, one rule at the one shared seam, and the rival scorer's dial_recipe reads the same number.

MEASURE FIRST: campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0 --ticks 40 (tags diag-ind, diag-anc are the 2026-09-02 traces) with the expenditure/income split per tick; the done-when is the sprint's - operating-positive survivors that keep producing. Also owed: the agency's 'persistently loss-making' idle rule should read operating net at the recipe's own bid cap, not realised loss at the ceiling, or it will keep idling the buildings the cap is meant to save.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 (campaign_lapse debt instrumentation, industrial band, unwarmed, seeds 0/1 - build_gen/verify/lapse/debt-ind-s*/debt.csv): 129 of 129 debt entries are dominated by the EXPENDITURE flow, and in every one of them expenditure exceeded income over the four ticks before entry. But two differential runs re-order the levers. (1) Construction materials at market price are the FIRST wave: with resource_costs zeroed the early wave nearly vanishes (debtors at tick 20: 26 -> 4; median entry tick 22 -> 34), because a processor costs 25 steel at 8-10x base = 3-4k against a mine earning ~50/tick and the scorer builds through the boom. (2) The pool bids are NOT the drain: reservation_mult 0 changes nothing. (3) The tick-20 cliff is BL-746's, not this item's: with the industrial goods-upkeep draws zeroed there is no collapse at all. This item therefore drops to B and re-scopes to the two real purchase leaks - construction materials bought at the ceiling (the scorer's build tempo should price materials at the live market, and the cap here should bound them by the building's expected value) and processing inputs bought above the recipe's output value - AFTER BL-746 lands, measured on the same instrument.

items.author: Claude (campaign_lapse debt instrumentation, Ben's instruction to track every balance)
items.title: The industrial band goes dark at tick 20 - an unmet goods-upkeep draw decays every building to zero
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-02, campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0, seed 0). Between tick 20 and tick 21 active buildings fall 219 -> 40 and idle rise 18 -> 198 in ONE tick, with unstaffed 0, exhausted 0 and labour unchanged (118.5 -> 119.0). 77 of 95 corps go from active to zero-active that tick, almost all extraction corps, many with positive balances. The per-corp mean supply factor decays from 1.0 at tick 1 toward 0 and reaches it at tick 20: supply_decay_permille = 50 is 5% per tick of a 0..1000 factor, so a building whose goods-upkeep draw is never met hits zero output exactly 20 ticks after it starts. In the industrial band every extraction site draws power 0.25 + timber 0.05 + stone 0.05 per tick and every processor power 0.40 + timber 0.08 + stone 0.08 (BL-708, BL-738 stage 2); power is a GRID good that reaches only network-connected tiles, generation is 18 falling to 3 units against a demand of 64, and a generator short of power throttles itself. The ancient band has no such draw and takes the same debt wave without a cliff. DIFFERENTIAL PROOF: with the two industrial goods baskets zeroed the field holds 207-257 active buildings through tick 60, income runs ahead of inputs from tick 25, produced value 16-31k/tick, debtors 19 -> 5. Nothing else was changed.

WHY IT IS A DESIGN DEFECT AND NOT A TUNING ONE. PRODUCTION.md § A shortfall scales output; it never idles says the lights go dim, not out - but a factor that decays without floor DOES go out, and it goes out for every building the grid cannot reach, which is most of them. Three levers, and Ben's call which (NR-782): (a) a FLOOR on the supply factor (e.g. 0.5) so an unmet draw halves output and never zeroes it - the rule as the doc states it; (b) NO DRAW WHERE THERE IS NO WIRE - a building the network does not reach does not draw power and does not decay for want of it (it pays the no-grid penalty some other way, or none); (c) generation bootstrap - generators exempt from the power draw, and the draw switched on per building only once its market has ever priced power. (a) and (b) are one-line rules at the one shared seam; (c) is the census's own reading of BL-708. Then re-run the debt instrument: the done-when is no one-tick cliff and a field whose active count tracks its holdings.

MEASURE with: campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --seed N --warm 0 --ticks 60 --tag <tag>; corps.csv carries supply_factor_mean and bldg_supply_zero per corp per tick; world.csv buildings_active/idle. The 2026-09-02 traces are debt-ind-s0/s1 (the cliff) and exp-noupkeep (without it).

STAGE 1 LANDED 2026-09-02 (Ben approved NR-782 (a) and (b)). The floor: supply_floor_permille = 500 in economy.building_upkeep, parsed and range-checked like its siblings; run_building_upkeep decays to max(floor, factor - decay) and lifts a stranded factor to the floor. No wire, no draw: an unreached building's grid goods are struck from its basket before the shared draw (its ordinary goods still draw and bind), and an emptied basket draws nothing and counts as met. building_upkeep R8 (floor 500 holds at 500 over 41 ticks, recovers by the authored step, the number is the authored one, a factor below it is lifted) and R9 (an unreached building does not weaken for power on the grid; the same good off the grid decays 5 x 50; timber still binds on the unreached tile) - every row with its differential. RE-MEASURED (campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0 --ticks 60, tags fix-ind-s0/s1): no building at factor 0 at any tick; active buildings 224 at tick 20 and 221 at tick 60 (seed 0; was 219 -> 2), 178 and 137 (seed 1); income at tick 60 13.4k / 6.8k (was 132 / 2.9k); produced value 16.1k / 10.1k (was 262 / 2.0k); debtors 11 of 86 / 6 of 73 (was 22 of 66 / 13 of 58). The ancient band is byte-identical (19 entries, same table) - it has no draw to floor. Debt entries fall 67 -> 57 and 62 -> 58 and their shape changes: starved 32 -> 7, loss-converting 30 -> 42 - the residue is BL-745's.

STAGE 2 (open, NR-782 (c) held): the field's mean supply factor settles at ~0.57 - most buildings sit AT the floor because power still does not arrive (generation 18 -> 3 units against a demand of 64; a generator short of power throttles itself; only network-reached tiles can receive it). The generation bootstrap - generators exempt from the power draw, a building drawing power only once its catchment market has priced it - is the next lever, measured on the same instrument: the done-when is the mean supply factor climbing off the floor.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The Era -1 sim runs on the 1960 arc, as two spans on one engine with a boundary year between them
items.design:
THE GAP. Under epoch 1960 the polity sim does not run at all: era_minus_one.cpp gates on epoch_year < 1700, so the arc we are building the product on has ancient borders from the one-shot ladder and settlement passes and no simulated history behind them. The design (HISTORY.md § The epoch and the run, 2026-09-03) is two spans on one engine: an ancient pass to a BOUNDARY YEAR and an industrial pass from the boundary to the epoch.

THE WORK. (1) Widen the gate: the sim runs whenever prehistory_years > 0, at any epoch. (2) history_sim_params gains boundary_year, derived in era_minus_one.cpp as epoch_year - 400 by default (so a 1960 arc is 1560 -> 1960 for pass 2; pass 1 is whatever prehistory_years leaves before it); on an ancient epoch the boundary falls past stop_year and there is one span, byte-identical to today - assert that with world_determinism against the current golden. (3) The tick-band ladder applies per span: the stepped clock's whole point is that rounds concentrate near the END of a span, so each span carries its own bands rather than one ladder stretched over both. (4) The band a region builds and fields at is capped at Medieval in pass 1 and released in pass 2 - the roster gating is already cumulative (works_roster, unit_roster), so this is a ceiling on the band the polity may reach, not a new table. (5) history_sweep reports both spans.

DERIVED BOUNDARY (open, Ben's call): the year the first polity lights a furnace (run_settlement's furnace date) is the better-founded boundary than an authored offset. Build the authored default first; the derived one is a one-line swap once Stage 4 sits inside the run (BL-748, industrial pass ladder).

DONE WHEN: a 1960 world generates through both spans; the 0 CE world is unchanged; the generating-screen wait is measured and recorded on BL-754 (generation budget).

--- WHAT THE COLD REVIEW FOUND AFTER THIS LANDED, 2026-09-03 ---

The item's own DONE WHEN is met and independently verified in the main session: a 1960 world generates through both spans (1160 -> 1560 -> 1960, 800 years, deterministic), the 0 CE world is unchanged (digests 039EE9880739CDF6 / B0EBBA249B3DDABB / DE55600457797638 unmoved), and the wait is measured on BL-754. It is complete on those terms and stays complete.

Three things it did NOT do, each now owned elsewhere rather than left implied:

* BL-758 - running the sim at 1960 gives that arc ERA-SEEDED DEMOGRAPHY, because history_sim.cpp:332 seeds any zero-population region and settlement.cpp deliberately leaves 1960 regions at zero. era_world_harness R2 is red for that reason. The main session's verification missed it - world_determinism was green and that harness was never run. Ben's call, and the harness stays red until he takes it.
* BL-759 - every 1960-epoch instrument is re-based, so the sprint 33 baselines quoted from campaign_lapse describe a world HEAD no longer builds.
* BL-760 - the band ceiling has no behavioural observable, and the new save field has no round-trip assertion. R4 was downgraded to partial in consequence.

Also corrected here: BOTH spans tick at a flat 4 years. The design doc's "each span carries its own bands" is satisfied only in the weak sense that tick_bands holds two entries; the clock does not actually change between them. That was a deliberate first cut - the clock is not what the spans differ on, the roster ceiling is - and the tick ladder remains the tuning lever if the industrial span ever wants finer resolution.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Reach across water - Campaign and Settle across a sea leg, staged from harbour works, so colonisation by a major is the Metropole played overseas
items.design:
THE GAP. The sim knows enclosed-sea ring closure (w_ring) and nothing else about water: no Campaign or Settle target lies across a sea leg, so "the extent of colonisation by major powers" cannot be produced by pass 2 at all. The works roster already authors the rows that should gate it - Harbour Mole, Deepwater Wharf, Naval Yard, Coaling Station - and they do nothing for reach today.

THE DESIGN, in the sim's own currency. A sea leg is a candidate-grain extension of the target set: a region reachable by a coastal walk from a staging hub that holds a harbour work, with the leg's supply cost read from the same reach substrate the land term uses (one reach field, BL-325 ruling 3) and its range capped by the hub's best harbour row (Mole: littoral; Wharf: the enclosed sea; Naval Yard: open water; Coaling Station: any coast). Settle across the leg founds a holding that counts toward holdings_burden_q like any other - the burden of breadth is what makes an overseas empire strain, and reach-fed strain (COLLAPSE.md § 5, the Metropole's inevitability) is the accumulator it feeds. A colony is therefore expensive to hold and worth holding, and the major that holds too many culminates. Non-hegemony (BL-224, the non-hegemony invariant) is not relaxed for the sea: 1960 arrives multipolar.

BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION like the land verbs: two staging hubs per polity per round (the capital and one rotated coastal holding), candidate legs from those only. Deterministic - the coastal walk is over sorted tile indices.

DONE WHEN: history_sweep reports overseas holdings per major at the epoch and the distribution is wide; a polity with no harbour work never founds across water (asserted); world_determinism on the 0 CE arc unchanged.

--- WHAT THE SUBSYSTEM MAP FOUND, 2026-09-03 (amends the premise above) ---

THE PREMISE ABOVE IS WRONG IN ONE IMPORTANT WAY. "The sim knows nothing about water" is false. Region adjacency is water-blind at neighbour_radius 9, so short overseas campaigns are ALREADY legal and free (BL-755), and the Settle verb founds on ocean without a terrain test (BL-756). This item therefore PRICES AND GATES an existing capability; both prerequisites must be settled first, and the "before" figure for any sea-leg measurement is not zero.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, and cheaper than expected: the sim ALREADY HOLDS THE COASTLINE. sim_terrain_view::substrate (history_sim.hpp:81) is the raster substrate array in row*gw+col order, populated verbatim from tile.substrate by build_sim_terrain, and it carries ocean / lake / coast. A deterministic coastal walk is expressible on the EXISTING view with no signature change, no world& and no ECS access - which preserves the sim's deliberate world-free design (history_sim.hpp:70-75). The substrate is fixed at generation and nothing rewrites it (components.hpp:545-546), so a per-body walk may be precomputed once.

THE HARD CONSTRAINTS. (1) INTEGER FIXED-POINT ONLY in the decision path (history_sim.hpp:24-28); every campaign-era pathfinding structure (tile_traversal_cost, flood_field_for, body_reach_field, logistics_path) is float-valued and CANNOT be reused. (2) Price the leg inside campaign_supply (history_sim.cpp:572), never beside it - pricing supply in two places is the BL-318 defect the comment at 545-566 records. (3) is_sea (components.hpp:378), never is_water: the campaign era's crosses_ocean reads is_water and so flips on a single lake tile, which is what sea_leg_census exists to measure. (4) Adding a candidate to the scorer changes the argmax even when it never wins, so the ancient arc must be gated to execute identically or world_determinism's 0 CE digests move.

STILL OPEN, and needing Ben before this is buildable: which walk (coast tiles only vs all is_sea) and how the four harbour rows map onto ranges, given nothing in the code labels a sea "enclosed"; where the walk is anchored, since a region has no harbour tile and adding one is a save-format change; how "holds a harbour work" is tested, since work_row has no harbour flag; whether the naval roster rows (Coastal Galley, Broadside Ship, Ironclad - all base power 0 and skipped by sum_stack) gain real power here or stay inert; and whether an overseas daughter region re-surveys port_q instead of inheriting 0.7x.

--- LARGELY DISSOLVED BY THE WATER-DOMAIN RULING (Ben, 2026-09-06) ---

This item was to build a sea-leg candidate channel: a coastal walk, harbour rows mapped to ranges, a supply cost priced through campaign_supply. Under the water-domain model most of that falls out rather than being built. A "sea leg" is just a path whose domains require a naval traversal capability (BL-778), and the units that may take it are the naval rows made real by BL-779.

What survives of this item: the harbour works still want a reason to exist beyond reach_mod, and the question of whether a coastal province can hold a port is still open. The five design calls recorded above are mostly answered by the ruling - which walk, how the harbour rows map to ranges, and how "holds a harbour work" is tested all collapse into "which domains does this unit declare".

Re-scope or close this item before building it; it should not be built as filed.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: A polity chooses protection in the industrial pass, and the nation inherits it as an enacted import tariff at world setup
items.design:
THE LEVER. The import_tariff law (D4) exists and is inert at world setup - no tariff is enacted, so not one line of its arithmetic runs. The design (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Three passes, "separate market conditions are produced by in-world forces with visible causes") wants each nation's tariff posture to be a FACT OF HISTORY the player can read, not a per-nation dial. A nation that industrialised late relative to its neighbours protects what it has; one that industrialised first wants open markets.

THE DESIGN. In pass 2 (BL-747 two-span prehistory, BL-748 industrial pass ladder) a polity carries a protection scalar, moved deterministically by its industrialisation timing against its neighbours' (the axis derive_national_character already reads for ideology) and by whether it holds colonies (BL-749, sea-leg campaign: a metropole protects its ties). At handoff, a polity above the protection threshold enacts an import_tariff law on the campaign nation at world setup, rate banded off the scalar, author set so the transfer credits the nation's treasury as the law already specifies. Under the 2026-08-18 nation grant: a nation setting a tariff is exactly what the grant admits; pure, seeded, replayable, never a planner. Whether the polity carries it as a scored VERB (spend a round to raise protection) or as a DERIVED output read at handoff is Ben's call - the derived form is cheaper and is the default here; the verb form makes it a strategy weighting (BL-488, polity strategy weightings) and costs a candidate per round.

THE PLAYER'S HALF. The player's home market is sheltered because its nation's history sheltered it. That is the "supporting local companies in their initial sales" of the 2026-09-03 brief, done as a force with a visible cause.

DONE WHEN: a 1960 world opens with some nations tariffed and most not, the Law panel shows each one, and the tariff pass's own harness (law tests) is green with generated tariffs in place.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The warm start promoted to a generation pass - firms spawn and exit, banded coarse, until the field is operating-positive and steady
items.design:
TODAY app::start_new_game runs pre_game_ticks (80, ~20 years) then rebases the clock: a settling pass with no spawn and (since BL-743, firm exit) a cull. The design (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Three passes of simulated history, pass 3) makes it the pass that produces market conditions at game start.

THE WORK. (1) The settle becomes a world-generation step with its own params (settle_ticks, settle band, spawn cadence, stop test) rather than an app constant; harnesses derive it through the same helper as the app (the BL-462 discipline). (2) SPAWN: Pass 6 background-firm generation re-runs at a fixed cadence against the demand the field has now (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 6 recurs), so a niche opened by an exit re-fills. (3) CULL: firm exit as it stands. (4) STOP: operating-positive and steady - mean operating net positive and a majority of corps operating-positive across a trailing window, the campaign_lapse four metrics - with a hard tick cap. NEVER "every chain closed": stable is not saturated. (5) At the end of the pass assert the chain-completeness SPREAD (demand_census R5) so the settle cannot flatten the map. (6) Banded coarse: if cost demands it, a coarse band with scaled tick effects, the grain switch a pure function of sim state (the BL-492 banded-year-grain shape), asserted by the determinism harness.

PRECONDITION, not a neighbour: SPRINT 33's done-when, not sprint 31's. Sprint 31 closed 2026-09-02 a success on SOLVENCY - a majority of corps end thirty years operating-positive - and that is necessary but not what this pass needs. A settle selects over a field that must KEEP PRODUCING: valued production still falls across the run (x0.2 on seed 0, x0.6 on seed 1), so a longer settle on today's field would cull toward a smaller economy rather than a steady one. Gated on BL-746 (upkeep starvation cliff) and BL-745 (processor input bid cap), and on sprint 33 showing valued production flat or rising across the lapse.

DONE WHEN: campaign_lapse on a settled 1960 world shows the four metrics steady from tick 0 of play; the corp count at handoff is a consequence of the settle, not of the Pass 6 cap alone; the settle's wall clock is on BL-754 (generation budget).

--- SUPERSEDED IN SHAPE BY THE 2026-09-03 PHASE REORDER ---

Ben's point 8 retires the warm start rather than promoting it, and his point 6 replaces the settle with a DIRECTED PARALLEL CANDIDATE SEARCH over 1560-1960 (BL-770). This item was the warm start promoted - the same undirected pass, longer, with spawn and cull - and that is no longer the design. Do NOT build it as filed. Either rewrite it around phase 6 or close it superseded; BL-772 owns the retirement and BL-770 owns what replaces it. Its gate on sprint 33's growth half still applies to BL-770, for the same reason: a search over a field whose valued production falls will select the least-bad shrinking economy.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Pass 2's colonial ties seed the order book's preferred-seller relationships, so a colony's chains close through its metropole first
items.design:
THE LEVER. The order book already honours a buyer's preferred_seller, served first and tolerated up to 1.10x the cheapest compatible ask (MARKETS.md step 10). Nothing sets it at generation. Pass 2 (BL-749, sea-leg campaign) produces ownership history - which metropole held which colony, and for how long - and that is exactly the fact a trade tie should be derived from.

THE DESIGN. At handoff, for each region that was an overseas holding at the epoch or within N years of it, firms placed there carry a preferred_seller toward the metropole nation's firms for the goods the colony cannot close itself (the chain-completeness read says which). A tie, not a rule: the 1.10x tolerance is the whole strength of it, and a cheaper local seller beyond that tolerance wins. This is the third of the three forces in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Three passes - tariffs, distance, ties - and the one that makes "global trade" a set of ROUTES with a history rather than a uniform pull toward the cheapest ask.

DONE WHEN: haulage_measure on a 1960 world shows convoy traffic on colony<->metropole legs above the baseline; removing the ties (params) removes it; determinism unchanged.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: One seed-sweep instrument for the three passes - chain-completeness spread, the lapse four, the haulage baseline, the sweep distributions - read as distributions, never as per-world targets
items.design:
"GAMIFYING GENERATION" MEANS A SCOREBOARD, NOT A TARGET. Ben, 2026-08-31: no start is clamped up to viability or down to fairness; generation owes the SPREAD. The three passes are tuned by moving a force (a weight in history_sim_params, a tariff threshold, the settle's spawn cadence) and reading how the DISTRIBUTION across a seed spread moves. The instruments exist and are read one at a time; this item puts them on one sheet.

THE WORK. A sweep target (run_sweep.cmake already fans harnesses over seeds) that, per seed, records: chain-completeness spread (demand_census R5 - min, median, max, tails); the lapse four at handoff (mean operating net, operating-positive corps, valued production, debtors); the haulage baseline (convoy count and cargo vs the 1055/802 reference - goldens cannot see trade); and history_sweep's pass-1/pass-2 outputs (nation count, furnace years, overseas holdings, tariffed nations). One table, seeds as rows, printed and diffable. No assertion beyond "the spread is not zero" - the instrument reports, the sprint argues.

DONE WHEN: the sheet exists, runs over the standard seed spread in one command, and sprint 32's retro cites it.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The generating-screen budget for three passes - measure first, then re-file only the affordability rungs the measurement demands
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-03: "I am interested to see if this can be done cheaply. This is in fact a difficult abstraction problem." The budget is the generating screen's wait (~25-38 s generation + ~6 s warm start today, per app.cpp). Pass 1 is already the most expensive pass; pass 2 doubles it and pass 3 lengthens the settle by an order of magnitude at 4 ticks a year. Cost tracks the province table, not the fighting (COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem).

THE WORK. (1) Instrument the wait per pass on the loading screen's progress sink and in history_sweep, so every sprint-32 item records its cost on this item as it lands. (2) The affordability rungs in COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem - kill the O(provinces) scans, quiet-province fast path, banded year grain, record on change - were purged with the ancient pivot and are NOT re-filed here in advance. Re-file the one the measurement points at, when it does, in that order. (3) The abstraction question Ben names is the handoff between two engines, not either engine: keep the handoff a struct of plain outputs (regions, works, strain, ties, posture) so pass 3 never reads pass 2's internals.

DONE WHEN: a 1960 world with all three passes generates inside a budget Ben has stated on this item; if it cannot, the item records which rung buys it back and that rung is filed.

--- MEASURED 2026-09-03, the instrumentation half landed with BL-747 ---

  0 CE, 400 y      total 8200 ms = pre-settlement 443 + settlement 4 + ERA-1 323 + post-era 7428
  0 CE, no era     total 6661 ms = pre-settlement 455 + settlement 3 + ERA-1   0 + post-era 6202
  1960, two-span   total 7996 ms = pre-settlement 465 + settlement 2 + ERA-1 197 + post-era 7331

THE ANSWER TO BEN'S QUESTION IS YES, AND BY A WIDER MARGIN THAN EXPECTED. The second span is not merely affordable, it is FREE: 800 simulated years at epoch 1960 cost 197 ms against 323 ms for 400 years at 0 CE, and the whole 1960 world builds FASTER than the 0 CE one. The reason is the one COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem already states - cost tracks the province/region table, not the fighting or the years - and at 1960 the settlement pass has already founded most regions, so the sim founds 506 where the ancient arc founds 833.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES BUDGETING. The era pass costs about FOUR TIMES its own wall clock. Era on versus off at 0 CE is a ~1.5 s difference, of which only 323 ms is the sim itself; the remaining ~1.2 s is every pass after it working over the 833 regions the era founded. A budget taken off the era's own timer is wrong by 4x, and the affordability rungs in COLLAPSE.md are aimed at the 323 ms rather than the 1.2 s.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE REMAINING RUNGS. None of them is needed yet. The 4000-year ladder (BL-494) is the case that would test them, and the right next measurement is a 4000-year ancient span at epoch 1960 rather than any optimisation. Do not re-file a rung until a measurement points at it.

STILL OPEN on this item: the budget Ben will actually state, and the settle pass's own cost (BL-751), which is gated on sprint 33.

--- TWO GAPS FOUND IN THE PLAY BUILD, 2026-09-03 ---

(1) THE GAME NEVER REPORTS ITS OWN GENERATION BUDGET. The "[gen budget]" line added with this item is inside the "if (fixture)" branch in hard_coded_world.cpp, and the app passes fixture = nullptr. So every number this item quotes is a HARNESS number, and the loading screen - which work item (1) explicitly named as the place to instrument - still says nothing about where its wait goes. Remaining work on this item, not a completed half.

(2) THE BUDGET IS NOT WHERE THIS ITEM WAS LOOKING. Measured in the release play build, the warm start is 72-73 s on BOTH arcs against generation's ~8 s. The pass this item exists to price (197-323 ms) is under half a percent of the startup wait. That does not make the era measurement wrong, but it does mean "can generation afford more complexity" is the wrong question to ask of the startup budget: generation is not what the player is waiting for. BL-761 owns the warm start.

items.author: Claude (sprint 32 subsystem map, 2026-09-03)
items.title: The Era -1 campaign already crosses open water, unpriced and ungated - sea reach is not absent, it is free
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the sprint 32 subsystem map, while scoping BL-749 (sea-leg campaign). It inverts that item's premise and must be understood before it is built.

THE FACT. Region adjacency is precomputed by the O(n^2) loop at history_sim.cpp:358-363 over region_distance (204-212), which is integer Chebyshev max(|dc|,|dr|) with wrapped columns - PURELY GEOMETRIC AND WATER-BLIND. With neighbour_radius = 9 (history_sim.hpp:262), a campaign target up to nine tiles across open ocean is ALREADY a legal candidate, scored and fightable, with no harbour work, no naval unit, and no supply penalty for the water. campaign_supply (572-586) prices hub distance and the terrain reach term; rebuild_reach's per-node tile_cost (374-387) reads LANDFORM ONLY, so a water anchor costs the same as plains.

WHY IT MATTERS. BL-749 is written as "the sim knows nothing about water, so colonisation cannot be produced". The truth is the opposite and worse: short overseas conquest is already happening for free, and every tuning constant in history_sim_params was measured with it happening. So BL-749 is not ADDING a capability, it is PRICING and GATING one that exists - and the "before" number for any sea-leg measurement is not zero.

THE WORK IS TO DECIDE, not yet to code. Either (a) the water-blind radius is the intended abstraction and the sea leg is a separate priced channel layered on top, or (b) adjacency should test water and the existing free crossings are a defect to close - which would move every polity's decision set and change every generated world, ancient arc included. (b) is a determinism-visible change and needs Ben's call. Measure first: instrument how many campaigns and conquests in a standard 400-year run cross a water tile between hub and target, and report it on the sweep before touching anything.

NOT a review-queue entry: this is work somebody must do, and the call it needs is stated above rather than filed as a question.

--- MEASURED 2026-09-03 (tools/verify/sim_water_census.cpp) ---

43% of the sim's adjacency edges cross SEA: 88,994 of 203,294 across 3 seeds, at neighbour_radius 9. Per seed 54% / 22% / 57%. So nearly half of every campaign target the sim can see is across water, reachable for free, with no harbour, no naval unit and no supply penalty.

THE "BEFORE" FIGURE FOR ANY SEA-LEG WORK IS THEREFORE 43%, NOT ZERO. BL-749 is not adding overseas reach; it is pricing reach that already dominates the map. And every tuning constant in history_sim_params - w_farm through the burden of breadth - was fitted with that free crossing happening, so pricing it will move the balance those constants were measured against.

The spread across seeds (22% to 57%) is wide enough that any seed sweep should carry this figure: two worlds can differ by a factor of nearly three in how much of their campaign space is overseas.

--- SUPERSEDED IN SHAPE BY THE WATER-DOMAIN RULING (Ben, 2026-09-06) ---

This item framed free sea crossing as a PRICING problem - 43% of adjacency edges crossing water with no supply penalty. Ben's ruling makes it a LEGALITY problem instead: a unit type declares which domains it can cross, so a land stack simply cannot enter unowned water. That is cheaper to reason about than a penalty and cannot be tuned into meaninglessness.

BL-778 (unit traversal domains) owns it. The 43% measurement stands as the before figure and should be re-read against the new legality rather than against a cost.

items.author: Claude (sprint 32 subsystem map, 2026-09-03)
items.title: The Settle verb applies no terrain test, so a polity can found a region on an ocean tile - and that region is silently undefendable
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the sprint 32 subsystem map. A prerequisite for BL-749 (sea-leg campaign), which cannot assert "a polity with no harbour work never founds across water" while founding on water is unconditionally legal.

THE FACT. The Settle verb's ring probe (history_sim.cpp:1160-1180) checks only whether another region already occupies the candidate cell (1176-1178). There is no substrate test, so an ocean cell is a legal founding site. The consequence is not cosmetic: sub_at(terrain, np.anchor) then hands resolve_battle a water substrate, and terrain_combat.cpp:87-89 returns 0 defence and 0 forage for every water kind, so a region founded on water is silently undefendable and unforageable. Nothing reports it.

A SECOND, RELATED FACT worth carrying with it: region::port_q is not sea access. survey_endowment counts is_water tiles - LAKES INCLUDED - over a neighbourhood window (settlement.cpp:166,180,199), and a founded region never re-surveys, inheriting 0.7x the parent's value (history_sim.cpp:1193). So port_q is a decayed wetness fraction, and any harbour-work or sea-leg gate keyed on it gates on the wrong thing. Whatever BL-749 tests for sea access must be a real is_sea test at the anchor (components.hpp:378, which excludes lakes), not a port_q threshold.

THE WORK. Add the land test to the Settle probe, and a harness row that asserts no region in a full run sits on water. MEASURE FIRST and report the count in a standard 400-year run: if foundings on water are common the fix moves every world, ancient arc included, and world_determinism's 0 CE digests will change - which makes it Ben's call to take, not a quiet correctness fix. If the count is zero the test is a cheap guard and lands free.

--- MEASURED 2026-09-03 (tools/verify/sim_water_census.cpp), and it is FAR bigger than this item assumed ---

Across 3 seeds, generation's own era: 1105 of 3819 regions sit on WATER at their anchor - about 29% - and 982 of those on SEA proper rather than a lake. Per seed: 392 of 1333, 243 of 1284, 470 of 1202. Of them 233 / 99 / 281 sit on OPEN OCEAN.

THE MEASUREMENT WAS VALIDATED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. region::anchor is documented as row*gw+col (settlement.hpp:76), the sim writes it that way on every founding (history_sim.cpp:1193), and the harness indexes the same raster. The consequence is confirmed at history_sim.cpp:1056, where resolve_battle is handed sub_at(terrain, tgt.anchor) - so a region anchored on ocean genuinely fights on a water substrate, and terrain_combat returns 0 defence and 0 forage for every water kind.

SO THIS IS NOT AN EDGE CASE. Roughly three regions in ten, in every world, are undefendable by construction, and nothing reports it. This item guessed "if the count is zero the test is a cheap guard and lands free". It is not zero, so the guard is the opposite of free: adding a land test to the Settle probe would remove ~29% of every world's regions, move every downstream pass that reads the region table, and require re-blessing world_determinism. THAT IS BEN'S CALL, and a much larger one than the filing suggested.

It also varies strongly by seed (18% to 39% of regions), which is the kind of asymmetry the design wants - but unpriced and unintended.

--- SUPERSEDED IN SHAPE BY THE WATER-DOMAIN RULING (Ben, 2026-09-06) ---

This item proposed a land test on the Settle probe - deleting every region on water, measured at ~29% of all regions. Ben's ruling makes most of them LEGITIMATE instead: coastal water is owned by whoever owns the shore, so a region founded there has an owner to belong to. Only open ocean is unowned.

So the fix shrinks from ~1105 regions to the ~613 anchored on open ocean, and it stops being a deletion and becomes a founding rule. BL-777 (region domain) owns it. Do NOT build this item as filed.

items.author: Claude (measured on the pre-change tree, 2026-09-03)
items.title: history_sweep sweeps the struct default, not the era generation runs - BL-462 unclosed in the one harness whose whole job is the era
items.design:
MEASURED 2026-09-03, on the tree before any sprint 32 change, by running ./build_gen/verify/history_sweep.exe.

THE FACT. The report prints its own span in its header: "=== history sweep (BL-275) - 16 seeds, -4000 -> 0 ===". Generation runs -400 -> 0. The cause is one line: history_sweep.cpp:314 constructs a default history_sim_params - the bare struct default, six bands and 136 rounds - and never calls era_minus_one_sim_params(world_params). Line 272 does the same for the header. So every distribution the sweep reports (province counts, powers, hegemony rate, battles, conquests, peak population, works raised) describes a 4000-year six-band run that no world is ever generated from.

WHY THIS IS THE BL-462 DEFECT AND NOT A NEW ONE. era_minus_one.hpp exists to stop exactly this: its header lists six axes on which a re-derived invocation diverges from generation, and HISTORY.md states "Every harness derives its parameters through the same helpers, so no check measures a different run from the one that generates a world (BL-462)". That sentence is false for history_sweep, which is the harness the design leans on hardest - COLLAPSE.md and HISTORY.md both name it as the place every magnitude in the Era -1 layer is argued. era_minus_one.hpp:49-57 already records that BL-462's scope missed a caller nobody counted; this is a second one.

A SECOND READING IS DEFENSIBLE and should be settled rather than assumed: the 4000-year ladder is the stated TARGET (BL-494, four-thousand-year ladder) and the 400-year band is a placeholder, so sweeping the default ladder may be deliberate research rather than an error. If so the harness must SAY so on its face and offer generation's run too; a report that silently describes a different sim is the "instrument that cannot see its subject" pattern BL-714 groups.

THE WORK. Give the sweep an --epoch flag that builds a world_params and derives through era_minus_one_sim_params, so it can measure generation's real run; keep the default-ladder sweep as an explicitly labelled second mode. Print the params actually used - start, boundary, stop, band count, rounds - in the header of both.

OBSERVED ALONGSIDE, needs confirming rather than acting on: the same run raised ZERO works across all 16 seeds with the works fixture enabled (the works column read 0 on every row). Either the fixture gates never fire or build_work never wins the scored contest. If build_work never wins, the works roster is inert and BL-748's band unlock has nothing to unlock - which would make this a much larger finding than a mislabelled header.

--- DELIVERED 2026-09-03 (sprint 32 wave 2) ---

The sweep now measures generation's own era on the --epoch path, via era_minus_one_fixture rather than by reconstructing the arguments - which is the route era_minus_one.hpp's header was written to make possible and history_conquest_gap already used. All six divergence axes closed on that path; the default ladder path is untouched and still labelled as research.

THE CHECK THAT MATTERS IS SELF-CHECKING. New row S1b requires the re-run to reproduce generation_report's own prehistory_battles/conquests/foundings, per seed. That cannot rot the way a pinned 270/207/833 would.

TWO RESIDUALS, both real and neither hidden:
* Generation is still called with works = nullptr here (as world_determinism does). The APP passes its real registry, so the shipped game scores FIVE verbs where every harness scores four. That divergence was flagged by the BL-747 implementer and is now doubly confirmed; it is axis 5 and it is not closed.
* Works-per-band is end-state only. Splitting it either side of the boundary year needs the sim to timestamp each work, which is a sim change. R4 is partial for both reasons.

ALSO CORRECTED HERE: the banner written earlier the same day said "seed, creeds, works and settlement still diverge", which was honest when the params-only fix landed and understated once the fixture route did.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, 2026-09-03. (1) history_sweep.json was NOT stale. The BL-747 implementer reported "seed 0: regions_end 2115 committed vs 2095 now" and I repeated it in a commit message; diffing the committed artifact against a fresh 16-seed default run shows regions_end 2095 in BOTH, and the ONLY field that differs across all 16 rows is `ms`. The substance is identical and the earlier claim was wrong. (2) That `ms` field is itself a small defect: it makes a committed artifact diff on every run for a reason unrelated to its subject, so a genuine drift is hidden in timing churn. Either drop the timing from the JSON or stop committing the file.

items.author: Cold review of the BL-747 diff, 2026-09-03
items.title: The 1960 arc now gains era-seeded demography as a side effect of BL-747, and era_world_harness R2 is red because of it - a design-red for Ben, not a harness to re-bless
items.design:
FOUND by the cold review of BL-747, 2026-09-03. The main session's own verification MISSED it: world_determinism was green and era_world_harness was never run.

THE CHAIN. era_minus_one_enabled now returns true at epoch 1960, so run_history_sim runs there. history_sim.cpp:332 unconditionally seeds every zero-population region (population = region_carrying_capacity(farm_q) / 8). settlement.cpp:544 deliberately leaves 1960-epoch regions at population 0 - the antiquity branch is the only seeding path. So 1960 regions go from 0 to roughly carrying capacity, and era_world_harness R2 ("the 1960 world stays demography-unseeded, graduation not its path") fails: 12 passed, 1 failed.

IT IS WIDER THAN ONE HARNESS ROW. That population feeds generate_population_centres (hard_coded_world.cpp:679), derive_national_character, and nation and corporation generation. The 1960 world's demography, politics and corporate seeding all move. HISTORY.md, the BL-747 requirement rows and the diff comments are all silent on it.

WHY IT IS BEN'S CALL AND NOT A FIX. Two defensible readings. (a) It is CORRECT and intended: the sim ran, it founded 506 regions, and regions with people are what a run produces - the harness asserts a property BL-747 deliberately overturns, and should be re-aimed with the change recorded in HISTORY.md. (b) It is a SIDE EFFECT nobody asked for: BL-747's subject is the span structure, and silently re-basing 1960 demography is scope the item never claimed. Under (b) the seeding should be gated so it only fires where settlement left the regions unseeded by design.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE HARNESS TO PASS. It is red for a real reason and stays red until Ben rules. Whichever way it goes, the 0 CE arc is unaffected - world_determinism's three digests are unmoved either way.

CONFIRMED IN THE MAIN SESSION 2026-09-03, not taken on the reviewer word. Built era_world_harness on the committed tree (build_lua_harness.bat, Release path) and ran it:

  PASS  R2 every 0 CE region holds population within (0, capacity]
  PASS  R2 manpower sits within its population ceiling
  FAIL  R2 the 1960 world stays demography-unseeded (graduation not its path)
  12 passed, 1 failed

So the 0 CE half of R2 is untouched and only the 1960 clause moved, which is exactly what the chain predicts and narrows the question to the one Ben has to answer. The harness is LEFT RED.

items.author: Cold review of the BL-747 diff, 2026-09-03
items.title: Every 1960-epoch measurement instrument is silently re-based by BL-747 - the sprint 33 baselines were taken before the era ran there
items.design:
FOUND by the cold review of BL-747, 2026-09-03.

THE FACT. campaign_lapse.cpp:386-389 with --epoch 1960 and without --fast now runs an 800-year era pass where it previously ran none, and that pass founds 506 regions. Every number quoted from that instrument at epoch 1960 was measured on a world the code no longer builds.

WHAT IS AFFECTED, by name: BL-745 (processor input bid cap) quotes "active buildings 224 at tick 20" and the 1.5-2.5x expenditure/income trace; BL-746 (upkeep starvation cliff) quotes the tick-20 cliff and the 18 -> 3 power figures; sprint 33's done_when is written against the same four metrics; BL-708's income-at-tick-60 figure. None of them is WRONG about the code it measured - they are simply no longer reproducible from HEAD.

THE WORK. Re-run campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 on the post-BL-747 tree and restate the sprint 33 baselines against it, BEFORE any sprint 33 item is judged against its old numbers. Cheap, and the alternative is a sprint measuring its progress against a world that no longer exists.

A NOTE ON WHY THIS WAS NOT CAUGHT: nothing links a code change to the instruments whose baselines it invalidates. That is the same class as BL-757 (a harness measuring a different run) and is worth a standing habit rather than a one-off fix - when a change moves world generation, the items quoting generation-derived baselines are part of its blast radius.

items.author: Cold review of the BL-747 diff, 2026-09-03
items.title: The two-span band ceiling cannot be observed changing a decision, and the new save field has no round-trip assertion
items.design:
FOUND by the cold review of BL-747, 2026-09-03. Two gaps of the same kind: a thing is set but nothing can see it working.

(1) THE CEILING IS UNOBSERVABLE. history_sim_state::works_raised is a single scalar with no band split, and no roster-band figure is reported anywhere, so nothing in the project distinguishes span1_band_ceiling = medieval from = industrial at epoch 1960. If no polity reaches materials capacity 4 before the boundary the clamp never binds and every check stays green. Requirement R4 of two-span-prehistory was marked complete on substituted evidence and has been downgraded to partial because of this. THE WORK: report works raised and units fielded PER BAND, either side of the boundary, and assert only that the ancient span raises nothing above medieval. Note this is entangled with BL-757's zero-works finding: build_work never wins the scored contest, so works-per-band may report zeros for a different reason.

(2) THE SAVE FIELD IS UNASSERTED. save_envelope_roundtrip.cpp:224-226 (S3, "world_params survives") checks only seed, abundance and epoch_year. prehistory_years was already unasserted and industrial_years now joins it - and since both default to 400, even a swap of the two round-trips clean. The write and read orders ARE correct (verified by the cold review), but they are guarded by a comment rather than a check, on a record whose version was just bumped to 4. THE WORK: assert every world_params field in S3, with the two year fields set to DIFFERENT non-default values so an order swap fails.

(3) SMALLER, same class: build_stack's ceiling = roster_band::industrial default argument (history_sim.cpp:167) is now dead - both call sites pass it explicitly. It is contained to an anonymous namespace, but a new in-TU caller would silently un-apply the ceiling with no diagnostic. Either drop the default or assert there are exactly two callers.

items.author: Claude (measured in the play build, 2026-09-03)
items.title: The warm start is 72 seconds on BOTH arcs - 12x its budget, and it dwarfs everything generation does
items.design:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 in the RELEASE play build (build_rel), running the app twice with --autostart:

  epoch 1960 (two-span)   warm_start_80_ticks  73167 ms   convoys 14763.9 | run_economy_step 57023.9
  epoch 0    (ancient)    warm_start_80_ticks  72088 ms   convoys 28321.1 | run_economy_step 42361.6

THE HEADLINE: THE TWO ARCS COST THE SAME, so this is NOT caused by BL-747. The 0 CE arc is byte-identical across that change (digests unmoved), and it pays 72.1 s where the new two-span 1960 arc pays 73.2 s. The warm start was already this expensive; running the sim at 1960 added roughly a second. Filed separately from BL-754 for exactly that reason - it is the startup cost the player actually waits through, and it belongs to the economy tick, not to generation.

THE SCALE OF THE MISMATCH. app.cpp's own comment budgets "the ~25-38 s generation plus ~6 s warm start that follow it". The warm start is running at 12x that. And it dwarfs the thing this sprint has been optimising: the Era -1 sim is 197-323 ms, generation end to end is ~8 s in the Release harness path, and the warm start is 72 s. Any conversation about whether generation can afford more complexity is answered by this number - generation is not where the startup budget goes.

WHERE IT GOES, and the two arcs split differently, which is the useful part:
  * run_economy_step dominates both, but MORE on the industrial band (57.0 s vs 42.4 s) - more recipes, more buildings, deeper chains.
  * convoys are the reverse (14.8 s industrial vs 28.3 s ancient), which is worth understanding on its own: the ancient arc spends nearly twice as long moving goods. Candidate cause is the ancient chain being shallower, so more raw tonnage moves further, but that is a hypothesis and not a measurement.
  * Everything else is noise: clear_markets ~0.11 s, apply_budget ~0.77 s, history_recorders ~0.39 s.

THE WORK, in order. (1) Profile run_economy_step across the 80 warm ticks and find what is O(n^2) or rebuilding per tick - 42-57 s over 80 ticks is 530-710 ms PER TICK, which is also what the player pays per tick at speed once playing, so this is a play-speed problem wearing a loading-screen costume. (2) Same for the convoy pass. (3) Only then consider reducing pre_game_ticks, which would be treating the symptom - the settle wants MORE ticks, not fewer (BL-751 makes the warm start a real generation pass).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WAIT: BL-751 (economic settle pass) proposes lengthening this pass by an order of magnitude so firms spawn and exit until the field is steady. At 0.9 s a tick that is not affordable, and BL-751's gate should read this item as well as sprint 33's growth half.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 1 - deposits split by ORIGIN: metals seeded with the body, biological resources deferred to the Life phase
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 1): "In this phase we should also seed simple resource deposits. For example metals." Metals are lithospheric and belong with the body; coal, timber and oil are the biosphere's residue and belong to Life (BL-765).

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and it is more than half the job. The split is ALREADY ENCODED, but as scattered gates rather than a table: planetology S8 (planetology.cpp:1413-1512) gates coal on peak life reaching land (:1455), petroleum on oxygenation (:1450), peat and timber and agricultural_produce on life still being present (:1457-1463). Fossils key off st.peak and living resources off st.stage, which is exactly why a dead world keeps its coal and loses its forests. generate_deposits is a PURE function of (substrate, cover, density, landform, two seeded streams, rarity) - tile_generation.cpp:1215, and the ore-field pre-pass already REPLAYS it exactly (:1793-1810) to build a bears mask, so replaying a subset is proven machinery, not a hope.

WHAT IS MISSING. (1) A resource ORIGIN classification. Nothing in src/ answers is_biological(resource_type) - the roster groups by source location and tier, RESOURCES.md by production tier and value track, and neither axis is geological vs biological. The only biotic predicate is is_biotic_cover(), which classifies COVER. (2) Endowment is a scalar MULTIPLY, not a placement - it can zero a resource but cannot say WHERE it goes.

THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS SUBSTANTIAL RATHER THAN SMALL. tile_rng is SHARED past the deposit call: the endemic amount draw (tile_generation.cpp:1934) and derive_environment's hazard/habitability jitter (:1949) consume it after the deposits do. So removing a draw from the deposit block MOVES HAZARD AND HABITABILITY on every tile - a world-changing edit dressed as a refactor. Either keep the biological draws in place and consuming (writing zero), or re-cut the stream deliberately and re-bless the 0 CE digests as a stated act.

DONE WHEN: a resource_origin table exists and is the single source of the geological/biological split; the Body phase places only geological deposits; world_determinism's 0 CE digests either hold, or move once with the movement stated and blessed on purpose.

--- PARTLY DELIVERED 2026-09-03 (sprint 32 wave 2), AND RE-SEQUENCED ---

DELIVERED: the classification, with a compile-time completeness guarantee. resource_origin plus resource_origin_of() - a switch with no default over all 49 resources - a constexpr table, and a static_assert that nothing survives as unset. Red-proofed by removing one case and watching every TU fail to build. So the implicit split that lived as six scattered gates in planetology S8 now has one home, and a new resource cannot be added without classifying it.

NOT DELIVERED, AND NOT DELIVERABLE HERE: moving the biological deposits out of the Body phase. That needs the Life phase to place them, and the Life phase (BL-765) needs BL-764, which is held back. Doing it now would generate a world with NO FOOD - survey_endowment reads agricultural_produce as a region's farm score, which drives cradle placement, region class, corporate focus and the whole food chain, and it reads coal+petroleum as energy, which gates industrialisation.

SO THE ITEM SPLITS along the seam it created: BL-762 owns the classification (done), BL-765 owns the move. R2 should be re-homed onto BL-765 rather than left open here. That is a correction to how the reorder was itemised on 2026-09-03, found by building it.

THE HAZARD IS STILL LIVE for whoever does the move: tile_rng is consumed past generate_deposits by the endemic amount draw and by derive_environment's hazard/habitability jitter, so the biological draws must keep CONSUMING (writing zero) rather than being deleted, or hazard and habitability shift on every tile. The digests are the tell.

ALSO: the static_assert message was written with an em dash and MSVC rendered it as mojibake in the build log. Made ASCII - a build error nobody can read is a worse guarantee than one they can.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 2 - continents gain a TIME AXIS: drift produces a sequence of plate positions, not just an endpoint
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 2, and his call on the form: SAMPLE REAL DRIFT HISTORY rather than a proxy). Coal has to go where the ancient swamps were, which means the generator must be able to answer "where was this ground, and what was it, at age T".

THIS IS THE FIRST OF THREE AND IT IS NEW MACHINERY, not a reorder. The feasibility pass returned BLOCKED-NEEDS-NEW-MACHINERY on the whole question, and this item is the least of the three gaps.

WHAT IS MISSING HERE. run_continents takes no age, no epoch count and no timestep, and returns no sequence. drift_col/drift_row are documented "per-epoch" but NO EPOCH LENGTH IS DEFINED ANYWHERE and no loop advances them - the drift vector exists and nothing integrates it.

WHAT IT WOULD COST, measured by the feasibility pass: the grid is 261x121 = 31,581 tiles and plate_count is 4-10, so one Voronoi snapshot is ~316k distance evaluations worst case plus two O(total) boundary walks. Replaying that for ~20 epochs is single-digit milliseconds. THE SNAPSHOT IS CHEAP; the expensive neighbour is the rift-basin search (corridor_of is O(total) per candidate pair, up to 45 pairs, with a 25-sample inlandness probe per corridor tile), which must NOT be re-run per epoch.

GOTCHAS. run_continents draws every plate's position, direction and oceanic flag from ONE shared stream in a fixed order (continents.cpp:68-84), so any new draw inserted in that loop shifts every subsequent plate and changes the world. And continent_state IS serialised (save_game.cpp:253-270) despite hard_coded_world.hpp:325-332 claiming it "never enters world, so it stays off the serialisation seam" - that comment is WRONG about the envelope seam and should be fixed with this item.

DONE WHEN: run_continents returns an ordered sequence of plate snapshots with a defined epoch length; the endpoint snapshot is identical to today's output so nothing downstream moves; the stale comment is corrected.

--- DELIVERED 2026-09-03 (sprint 32 wave 2) ---

The epoch is DEFINED: continent_epoch_years = 5,000,000 and continent_drift_epochs = 20 (100 My), both with their derivation in the header rather than as bare numbers. continent_snapshot_at reconstructs any past configuration by winding plate seeds back along their drift vectors and re-running the Voronoi.

THE SEQUENCE IS DERIVED, NOT STORED, and that is a deliberate departure from the item as filed. continent_state is on the save envelope seam; twenty plate_id rasters per body would be ~2.5 MB of save for data that is a pure function of five floats per plate. So run_continents' signature is unchanged and the sequence is snapshot_at over [0, depth].

WHY IT WAS SAFE TO ADD AT ALL: the snapshot consumes no randomness. The plate stream draws position, direction and oceanic flag for every plate in one fixed order, so a single inserted draw would have shifted every later plate and changed the world. Asserted by continent_drift C4, not assumed.

Verified by a new harness, tools/verify/continent_drift.cpp, ALL PASS: epoch 0 bit-identical to the present (C1 - the load-bearing row), 34% of tiles on a different plate at 100 My back (C2 - the axis moves real ground), reconstruction deterministic (C3), no randomness consumed (C4), a stagnant lid owning everything at every epoch (C5), and 0.24 ms per snapshot against 2.8 ms for the full pass (C6). world_determinism digests unmoved.

THE HARNESS IS AD HOC pending Ben naming it in .claude/skills/verifier-headless/SKILL.md - authoring the check is this session's, wrapping it as a skill is his call (DELIVERY.md, tool creation is skill creation).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and BL-764 still owns: ground does not ride its plate. plate_id at a past epoch answers "which plate seed was nearest this FIXED cell then", which is a reshuffling partition over stationary ground - not a tile that was somewhere else. Paleo-latitude is untouched: a tile's climate band is still its grid row. So BL-765 cannot yet ask "was this swamp".

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 2 - tiles ride plates, and a tile can be asked where it was and what its climate was at age T
items.design:
THE AIM: the second and deepest of the three gaps behind Ben's "realistically mapping the landform from ancient life to modern resources" (point 2). BL-763 gives drift a clock; this gives it a frame of reference.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM, and it does not go away by adding a loop. plate_id (continents.cpp:112) answers "which plate SEED is nearest this fixed grid cell". Tiles do not ride plates. Even with drifting seeds you get a Voronoi partition that reshuffles under stationary ground, not ground that moves - so "this tile was at the equator in the Carboniferous" is not expressible.

AND PALEO-LATITUDE IS THE SAME PROBLEM IN ITS SHARPEST FORM. Latitude is band_for_row(row) - THE GRID ROW ITSELF (tile_generation.cpp:314). A tile's climate band is fixed for all time by where it sits in the raster. There is no representation in which a tile HAD a different latitude, which is precisely what a coal-forming swamp at a tropical palaeolatitude requires.

THE THIRD GAP, PALEO-CLIMATE: nothing computes moisture, temperature or cover at a past epoch. theta_at (planetology.cpp:952) is the only past-state reconstructor and it returns a body-GLOBAL thermal scalar, not a per-tile climate. There is no climate_at(tile, age).

SCOPE HONESTLY. This is a representation change to the oldest layer in the generator, and every pass downstream reads its output. It is the single largest item in the reorder and should be split again at promotion rather than taken whole. A cheaper intermediate exists and was NOT chosen (a present-landform proxy, form option (b)) - Ben took the real one, so it is filed at its real size.

DONE WHEN: a tile can be asked for its position and climate band at a given age, deterministically; the present-day answer is identical to today's, so nothing downstream moves until BL-765 reads the past.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 2 - coal where the ancient swamps were, oil where the ancient seas were, timber where the forest is now
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 2): a Life phase that maps "ancient life to modern resources" over the real landform. This is the payoff item - BL-763 and BL-764 exist only to make it possible.

THE SHAPE. A sibling pass (the established extension pattern: every tile-layer extension lands as a sibling reading the shared generation_record, settled 2026-07-21) that runs AFTER planetology's biosphere chain and places the biological deposits BL-762 deferred. Each resource reads the epoch its formation belongs to: coal from swamp cover at the carboniferous-analogue epoch, petroleum from shallow-sea extent at its own, peat from present marsh, timber and produce from present cover. Fossils read PAST state, living resources read PRESENT - the same fossil/living split planetology S8 already encodes in its peak-vs-stage gates.

IT MUST BE A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A ROLL (Ben, standing: new generation stages are deterministic consequences of upstream scalars). The epoch a resource forms in is derived from the biosphere history, not authored per resource; the placement is derived from the paleo-climate at that epoch, not from a rarity draw.

WHAT ALREADY POINTS THIS WAY: ore-field siting ALREADY crosses the geological/biological line - coal's candidate test reads COVER (marsh, forest, grass) plus a land-height percentile (tile_generation.cpp:1004-1013), sitting in the same routine that sites porphyry copper off the convergent-boundary mask. So a coal field already asks a biological question; it just asks it of the PRESENT map.

DONE WHEN: coal, petroleum and peat are placed from the paleo record rather than from present cover; a world whose biosphere never reached land has no coal anywhere (already true via endowment, now true by construction); the distribution across a seed sweep is reported, not asserted.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 3 - the population map is drawn early and weighted by farming, then GROWN AND DESTROYED by history
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 3 and point 5, and his call on the form: DRAW EARLY, EVOLVE THROUGH HISTORY). "We should also draw the population map, giving extra attention to areas where farming would be easy", and city states count as population centres inside the History phase.

THIS DELIBERATELY OVERTURNS BL-610. Centres were moved AFTER the Era -1 sim (hard_coded_world.cpp:672-680) so that centre count and scale would be the history's consequence rather than a land-area divisor. Ben's ordering keeps that goal and gets it a better way: centres exist DURING the history and are grown, sacked and abandoned by it, so they are still history's consequence - and the sim stops running over a world with no cities in it, which is the defect the current order leaves.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is one thing more than it looks. (1) THERE IS NO CENTRE-REGION BINDING IN EITHER DIRECTION. region (settlement.hpp:74-159) carries anchor, col, row, population, manpower_stock - no entity id, no tile id, no centre list; the only mapping anywhere is a spatial nearest-search. (2) The sim has NO ECS access by design (history_sim.hpp:747-755: no world&, no tile ids, no entity allocator), so centres cannot be CREATED inside it without either breaking that property or representing them at sim grain and materialising them after. (3) sim_terrain_view carries substrate, cover, density and landform only - placement needs habitability and deposits, which are not in it.

THE RECOMMENDED SHAPE, given (2): represent centres at SIM GRAIN (a small struct on the region, integer, no entities) and materialise the ECS centres once after the sim, from that record. It keeps the sim world-free, keeps determinism integer, and still lets cities rise and fall.

SAVE FORMAT: two nested versions and neither migrates - world_save_version 23 covers population_centre_component, save_game_version 4 covers the envelope. A field on region bumps one, a field on the centre bumps the other. And r_popcentre validates each bool as exactly 0 or 1 and fails the whole stream otherwise; any new flag carries the same contract.

DONE WHEN: the farming-weighted map is drawn before the sim; the sim grows and destroys centres; the campaign-era centres are materialised from that record; a sacked city is visible as a smaller or absent centre at the epoch.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 4 - tune the forces until empires reliably form, grow and collapse, measured as a distribution and never clamped
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 4): "We definitely want to force outcomes where empires form, grow, and collapse. I think we should be able to select parameters that force empires forming."

THE READING IS SETTLED, and it was raised rather than assumed. On the elicitation form of 2026-09-03 Ben chose TUNE-FORCES-COMMON-OUTCOME over guarantee-by-reroll and over clamping the map: empires are to be a COMMON outcome across the seed spread, and a world with none is a legitimate outcome. That keeps three standing rulings intact - nation count emerges and is never tuned to a target (2026-07-30), no world is clamped up to viability or down to fairness (2026-08-31), and BL-224's non-hegemony invariant, under which every major must lose eventually and the epoch arrives multipolar.

SO THE WORK IS A TUNING LOOP, NOT A GATE. COLLAPSE.md already supplies the theory: collapse is INEVITABLE for a major, a deterministic consequence of upstream scalars, and the metagame is when it breaks, how it breaks, and who inherits. What is missing is that nothing measures whether a major ever RISES. The strategy roster (six shapes, BL-488's weightings) is authored and unmeasured.

WHAT TO BUILD: report, per seed, the largest polity's peak share of the map and the year it peaked, whether it then lost that peak, and which culmination resolved it. Then tune the verb weights until the rise-peak-fall shape is common across the spread. Report the distribution; assert only that the spread is not degenerate.

A PREREQUISITE THAT IS ALREADY FILED: this needs a sweep that measures the run generation actually performs, and today's does not (BL-757). Tuning against the struct-default ladder would tune the wrong sim.

DONE WHEN: the sweep reports the rise-and-fall shape per seed; empires are common across the standard spread and absent in some worlds; no world is inspected and adjusted.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 4 - simple roads stamped FROM the history, and markets emerging at the end of it
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 4): "We should also be laying simple roads to supply provinces. And markets should begin to emerge towards the end of this phase."

FEASIBILITY SAYS: DERIVE THEM FROM THE HISTORY, DO NOT LAY THEM INSIDE IT. Laying roads during the sim came back BLOCKED-NEEDS-NEW-MACHINERY for three independent reasons. (1) The sim has no write channel to the world - no world&, deliberately (history_sim.hpp:68-75). (2) It has no tile-grain route: its Dijkstra is region-to-region over the neighbour graph and returns a COST, never a tile list; the only thing that returns tiles takes world&. (3) generate_roads' node source is w.population_centre_tile, which is empty until after the sim. There is also a determinism idiom mismatch - the sim is integer fixed-point with no floats in the decision path, and edge_tier plus the redundancy rationing are float.

SO THE SHAPE IS: the sim RECORDS what it built (the works roster's road rows - Way Station, Span Bridge, Cut Canal - already represent exactly this), and a pass immediately after it STAMPS ancient-tier roads from that record over the settlement set. Same for markets: carve them at the end of the history phase from where trade actually concentrated, rather than from population alone.

THIS ALSO GIVES THE WORKS ROSTER SOMETHING TO DO. BL-757 measured zero works raised across sixteen seeds because build_work never wins the scored contest. Roads that visibly persist into the campaign are the first real payoff for winning it, and the scorer should be re-weighted with that payoff in view.

AN ERA-APPROPRIATE TIER RULE IS OWED: edge_tier and the rationing key off nation qualification percentile, a 1960-era field. Ancient roads need their own tier rule rather than borrowing the industrial one.

DONE WHEN: a 1960 world opens with roads whose shape follows the history's trunk routes; markets sit where trade concentrated; works raised is non-zero and its roads are visible on the canvas.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 5 - city states and pseudo-national borders become part of the History phase, so the history keeps its detail
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 5): "if we leave the consequence for after history, we lose detail in that history phase. I think it is fine to consider city states as population centres, and pseudo national borders as part of The History. I.e. you may have a Roman citizen, or an Athenian citizen."

WHAT CHANGES. Phase 5 stops CREATING the map and starts FINALISING what the history produced. The sim already writes region::nation as it goes, so pseudo-national borders exist inside it in embryo; what is missing is that they are not a political object a person can belong to. A citizen of a city state needs the centre (BL-766) and the polity to be the same kind of thing at sim grain.

THE NAMING RULE APPLIES AND IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. Ben's "Roman or Athenian" is the reader's analogy, not content: every generated polity, city and people is sci-fi/fantasy from the seeded banks. Real history is a mechanism reference, never a name source.

WHAT PHASE 5 KEEPS: generate_nations resolving the final territory from what the history left, derive_national_character reading its outputs, and the institutional record. What it LOSES: inventing the political map from region anchors as though the history had not just drawn one.

DONE WHEN: the History phase produces named polities and city states that the campaign inherits rather than re-derives; GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's phase table is rewritten around the new boundary.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 6 - a STATIC saturation search over candidate corporate landscapes, validated dynamically once
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 6): with roads, provinces, borders and markets already drawn by the history, phase 6 determines "what combination of companies/corporations makes a massive profit - and we should do this with multiple parallel candidate searches as a 1560 CE - 1960 CE pass".

TWO CALLS TAKEN ON THE FORM, 2026-09-03. (1) WHAT VARIES between candidates: corporation ROSTERS, starting PLACEMENTS, and ROAD/INFRASTRUCTURE TIERS - explicitly NOT whole upstream worlds, so generation runs ONCE and only the economic sim repeats. (2) THE OBJECTIVE is VIABLE-BUT-UNEVEN, not maximum profit. Maximising total profit would flatten the map that GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable exists to keep uneven; the search picks a landscape where profit is POSSIBLE and unevenly distributed.

THE BUDGET WORKS, AND ONLY BECAUSE IT IS PARALLEL. Measured 2026-09-03: 530-710 ms per economy tick, so 100 ticks at 4 years a tick is 53-71 s per candidate. Ben chose SIX candidates. Serially that is 5.3-7.1 minutes and breaks his 3-6 minute budget; in parallel on this machine's 16 logical cores it is ~1 minute of wall clock for all six. So the parallelism is not an optimisation, it is the reason the shape fits.

DETERMINISM IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE PARALLELISM. Each candidate must be a PURE function of (shared world, candidate seed, candidate parameters) with no shared mutable state, and the winner chosen by a deterministic argmax over a total order with an explicit tie-break - never by which thread finished first. Thread count must not change the result. Assert it: same seed, different thread counts, identical winner.

MEMORY: six live copies of a 31,581-tile world plus its entities. Measure it before assuming it fits.

DONE WHEN: six candidates evaluate in parallel inside ~1 minute; the winner is identical across thread counts; the chosen landscape scores viable-but-uneven on the chain-completeness spread rather than on total profit.

--- THE QUARTERLY-TICK RULING CHANGES THIS ITEM'S SPAN (2026-09-03) ---

Ben ruled the quarterly tick (NR-786), so phase 6 does NOT run at four years a tick. That leaves the span as the live question, because the item was filed against "1560 CE - 1960 CE" and that span is no longer free.

THE ARITHMETIC, at the measured 530-710 ms per tick:

  100 quarterly ticks =   25 years  =  53-71 s per candidate   <- fits the budget
  400 years           = 1600 ticks  =  14-19 MINUTES per candidate

Six candidates in parallel cost about one candidate's wall clock, so the first row fits inside Ben's 3-6 minutes with room and the second does not, by a factor of three even parallelised.

SO THERE ARE TWO WAYS TO HAVE PHASE 6, and they are not equivalent:

(a) 25 YEARS PER CANDIDATE, now. Enough to rank candidate rosters if the ranking stabilises inside 25 years - which is measurable and is the right first experiment: run one candidate for 200 quarterly ticks and watch when the ranking stops moving. Cheap, honest, available today.

(b) THE FULL 400-YEAR SPAN, after the per-tick cost is fixed. 530-710 ms per tick is itself the anomaly - BL-761 measured the warm start at 72 s for 80 ticks on BOTH arcs, twelve times what app.cpp budgets, and named run_economy_step and the convoy pass as the whole of it. If a tick came down to ~50 ms then 1600 ticks is 80 s per candidate and the full span fits. That is why BL-761 is now a REQUIRES on this item rather than a neighbour: it is the difference between 25 years and 400.

RECOMMENDED: build (a), measure where the ranking stabilises, and let that number decide whether (b) is worth buying. If the ranking settles in 15 years, the 400-year span was never needed and BL-761 stops being on this item's critical path.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the six candidates, the axes that vary (rosters, placements, road tiers), the viable-but-uneven objective, and determinism under threading - the winner comes from a deterministic argmax, never from completion order.

--- THE METHOD CHANGES: STATIC, NOT SIMULATED (Ben, 2026-09-03) ---

Ben restated the goal, and it is narrower than a market simulation: "the second epoch simulation is looking for groups of companies that ensure a market can continue trading... We're not looking for a 100% accurate series of trades to initialise resources, and neither what makes the most profit per tile. We want to find, given a planet with markets and national borders - how can we saturate all the resources in said market, so that each part makes some profit?"

THAT IS NOT A SIMULATION QUESTION. A tick answers "who traded what, at which price, this quarter". Saturation - every resource has a supplier and a buyer, every chain reaches a terminal sink, every participant clears its costs - is a STATIC PROPERTY of a candidate roster against a fixed world. Roads, borders, markets, deposits and population are all settled by the end of phase 4 and none of them changes during phase 6, so there is nothing to step.

AND THE MEASURES ALREADY EXIST (BL-775, which is now this item's prerequisite): measure_completeness returns terminals_closed / terminals_total per market from a static world, and recipe_margin computes revenue minus marginal cost from the registry alone. Between them they answer both halves of Ben's sentence.

THE ARCHITECTURE: EVALUATE STATICALLY, VALIDATE DYNAMICALLY, ONCE.
  1. Score every candidate roster as a coverage-and-margin problem - milliseconds each, no clock.
  2. Pick the winner by a deterministic argmax over a total order with an explicit tie-break.
  3. Run ONE short tick simulation on the winner alone, to confirm it holds up live.

That converts six candidates x 14-19 minutes into hundreds of candidates x milliseconds plus a single validation run. It also DISSOLVES THE SPAN QUESTION entirely - there is no span, because there is no clock - which supersedes the 25-years-versus-400-years arithmetic recorded above and makes BL-761 (the per-tick cost) irrelevant to this item's critical path.

THE ONE THING A STATIC CHECK WOULD MISS, and it must be carried explicitly: price feedback. Sprint 31's finding was that processors buy inputs at the CEILING and die - a dynamic effect that a base-price margin check cannot see, and it is the exact failure mode that killed the industrial field. The cheap proxy is a per-resource supply-to-demand RATIO per market: the ratio is static, and it is what drives a price to the ceiling in the first place. So the evaluator scores (a) terminal coverage, (b) per-firm margin at base, and (c) no resource left at a starvation ratio. The validation run in step 3 is what confirms the proxy was good enough.
